recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No further FHIR-core source work is needed for FHIR-17464 unless a future work group decision changes the search URL-processing model.
issue_request: FHIR-17464 was a Published FHIR-I change request resolved as Persuasive. It asked the search specification to clarify whether percent-encoded reserved separator characters are equivalent to raw separators and how that differs from FHIR's backslash escaping for literal search parameter values.
initial_application: The issue was applied by Git/SVN import commit e45b3e06685838ef5be827524cd4915ae0f9d214, titled "GF#17464 - clarifications about escaping" and carrying SVN revision 14562. That commit changed source/search.html's escaping section to distinguish code=a,b from code=a\,b and to state that FHIR backslash escaping operates at a different level from URL percent encoding.
additional_context: The linked Zulip thread confirms the rationale: percent encoding gets the search string across HTTP, while FHIR backslash escaping distinguishes search syntax from literal parameter content. Later FHIR-48702 added the top-level URL-encoding note and refreshed search examples, and FHIR-42834 corrected a same-section escaped-comma example; both related issues are already represented on the combined branch.
reconciliation: No source change was needed. Current source/search.html contains Notes on URL-Encoding and an Escaping Search Parameters section that says standard percent escaping still applies, shows equivalent percent-encoded URL forms, and separately shows that a backslash-escaped comma is literal data rather than a multi-value delimiter.
